Donald Trump, known for his not-so-cheery holiday messages, spent part of the very early hours of Thanksgiving morning lashing out at a New York Times reporter via his Truth Social platform.

The president took aim at David E. Sanger, the newspaper’s White House and national security correspondent, branding him in a 12:47 a.m. post “the mediocre reporter for the Failing New York Times” and “a lowlife that only writes what he is told to write by his bosses.”

Trump didn’t specify which article had drawn his ire, but Sanger published a piece on Wednesday titled “Trump Rejoiced in the Market’s Nvidia Surge. It Didn’t Last Long.”

In his post, Trump also reeled off a laundry list of purported accomplishments he complained Sanger failed to mention.

See Trump’s full post here:

The Times pushed back against Trump’s attack on the veteran reporter.

“David has covered five American presidents in more than four decades at The Times; his coverage of the ways in which the administration is shaping foreign policy and national security is unmatched,” Nicole Taylor, a spokesperson for The Times, said in a statement to HuffPost. “Noisy name-calling is just an attempt to distract from the news.”

It’s not the first time Trump has personally attacked the journalist.

In March, the president dismissed Sanger as a “lightweight analyst” from a “Failing” newspaper “that always gets it wrong.”

That outburst was prompted by Sanger’s analysis of a Trump post claiming the U.S. was close to fulfilling its objectives in its war on Iran and was now “winding down our great Military efforts in the Middle East.”

The war, which Trump launched in February, continues nine months later.

The Times defended its reporter at the time, with a spokesperson saying Sanger “brings more than 40 years of experience as a foreign and Washington correspondent for The Times — and a reputation for non-partisanship — to his work.”
